title: Model Provenance Taxonomy & Deployment-Readiness Index for Enterprise Buyers
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise buyers and internal Sales/Customer Success need a concise, actionable signal set to decide when a new open or third-party model is viable for Hosted/Dedicated/Private offerings. Current model tracking is ad-hoc: separate spreadsheets, intermittent Slack updates, and inconsistent note taking across vendor calls.

Goal: Create a reproducible taxonomy and a simple numerical 'Deployment-Readiness Index' (DRI) that aggregates provenance and enterprise suitability signals (license, training-data provenance, quantization compatibility, inferencing latency on target hardware, regulatory flags, vendor SLA/uptime claims, and commercial entitlements). The output should be a living dataset + a lightweight dashboard used by PM, Sales, and Solutions Engineering to make procurement and rollout decisions.

Deliverables: (1) Taxonomy doc describing signal definitions and collection priority; (2) ETL plan and scraper spec for automated signal ingestion from model repos, vendor pages, and benchmark runs; (3) DRI calculation notebook and CSV export; (4) One-page decision rubric for Sales & Solutions; (5) Prototype dashboard (Looker/Metabase or Redwood Console slice) showing current DRI across top 80 monitored models.

Why unique: This ticket emphasizes provenance (who trained it, what data types, license provenance) and deployment readiness (quantization and latency compatibility) together — a combination not present in our existing signal playbooks. It prioritizes enterprise procurement criteria rather than purely capability-based scouting.
acceptance_criteria: Taxonomy doc published in Confluence with clear definitions for at least 12 signals
Automated ingest spec for 3 sources (Hugging Face model card, vendor release notes RSS, CI synthetic benchmark outputs) reviewed and approved
DRI prototype script that produces CSV with model key and numeric score for 80 models
Dashboard prototype shows top 80 models, sortable by DRI and filterable by deployment suitability (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
Decision rubric signed off by Sales Lead and Solutions Engineering lead
